intro: Welcome to Göynük, a historic town in Bolu province, from the 18th–19th century. Whitewashed Ottoman houses step down the slope, and at the centre of the town stands the tomb of Akşemseddin.
history: Since the early Ottoman centuries, this town in Bolu had been a staging point. Its whitewashed, timber-framed houses, stepping down the slope, date from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. At its centre stands the tomb of Akşemseddin, tutor to Mehmed the Conqueror, and the settlement grew up around it.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the tomb of Akşemseddin and the bow-fronted houses. Visit the Süleyman Pasha mosque, and stroll through the old market.
facts: Did you know? Akşemseddin was both physician and sufi, and among the first Ottoman writers to hold that contagious disease spread by living things too small to see. The settlement grew around his tomb: the tomb of Akşemseddin, tutor to Mehmed the Conqueror.
outro: This brings our tour of Göynük to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This town has kept its character for centuries; let it keep it for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
